Synopsis:
You speak with the dead soul of a merchant, who was kidnapped by the mindflayers and died in the crash. The player can offer to help bury the body or perform any last rites, but they'll be rebuked by the spirit.

Cluster Contexts:
- CRA_DeadPrisoner_Dead.json: You have cast Speak with Dead on a merchant named Francis who was abducted by mindflayers during the shipwreck and later died in the crash; his corpse is before you and he appears as a weak, pallid shade. His replies are halting and fragmentary, limited to things he felt at the end—tentacles dragging him, “something” put in his eye, fire, screaming, and the crushing impact. The conversation assumes you already recovered his body and may offer burial or last rites, but the spirit rebukes such comforts and won’t sustain long explanations or new details. Expect gaps, broken hints, and short, choking answers rather than a full account.
- CRA_DeadFisherman2_Dead.json: You’ve cast Speak with Dead on a local fisherman who ran to the crash when he saw your ship fall from the sky. He insists he saw a mindflayer disguised as a beautiful woman and was then killed by Intellect Devourers — his words focus on sensory fragments (“brains,” “woman,” “beautiful”) rather than a full account. As with other Speak with Dead interrogations, his speech is choked and unreliable: replies are short, may trail off, and are limited to what he knew in his final moments, so expect gaps and few concrete details.
- PLA_TollCollector001_Dead.json: Speak with dead dialogue initiated when speaking to the decomposing corpse of a toll collector found in an abandoned tollhouse basement
- PLA_Refugee_Dead_PostEA.json: A speak with dead dialogue triggered when talking to the corpse of a refugee who was killed by gnolls. The dead man had signed a pact with an archdevil before his death.
- MOO_Oubliette_CorpseMembranes_Dead.json: The Speak With Dead dialog for the corpse hidden behind the mind flayer membranes in the bloodbath section of the Oubliette. This corpse is currently a goblin, but its race and backstory can be changed at the writer's behest.

Dialogue Excerpts (up to 3 samples, ordered):
Sample 1:
- Narrator: *The corpse regards you lifelessly.* (node 24)
- Player: What happened to you? (node 19)
- Abducted Nobleman: Guiding my cart... shadow fell... tentacle grabbed me... (node 20)
- Abducted Nobleman: Took me here... put something in my eye... (node 9)

Sample 2:
- Narrator: *The corpse regards you lifelessly.* (node 24)
- Player: Who are you? (node 27)
- Abducted Nobleman: Francis... merchant... selling pottery... (node 32)

Sample 3:
- Narrator: *The corpse regards you lifelessly.* (node 24)
- Player: How did you die? (node 23)
- Abducted Nobleman: Fire... screaming... then crunch. Nothing... (node 25)

context: You have used Speak with Dead on Francis, a merchant who was kidnapped by mindflayers during the shipwreck and later died in the crash; his corpse lies before you and his shade appears weak and pallid. His replies are halting, fragmentary, and limited to sensory impressions from his final moments—tentacles dragging him, “something” put in his eye, fire and screaming, then the crushing impact. Though you may offer to bury him or perform last rites, the spirit rebukes such comforts and will not sustain long explanations or reveal new, coherent details. Expect short, choking answers, gaps, and trailing-off lines rather than a full account.
